options.label: Media, data and society
options.labelReason: Media history and analysis, social theory, data analysis and AI ethics sustain the focus on media, data and society. Rhetoric, language and qualitative inquiry support communication study.
options.concept: Study how media and digital platforms shape what people see and how they participate. Combine media history, representation and rhetoric with data analysis, machine learning and AI ethics to investigate those effects.
progression: Media and rhetorical foundations precede later media analysis and applied rhetoric. Introductory data handling precedes machine learning. The brain and behaviour gateway precedes psycholinguistics and advanced research methods.

options.label: Media, communication and markets
options.labelReason: Media history, representation and storytelling combine with audience research, economics, marketing and digital strategy. These support media and market study with an emphasis on organisations and consumers.
options.concept: Study how media producers and organisations reach audiences. Combine media analysis with marketing, market research and digital strategy to investigate consumer decisions and how organisations respond.
progression: Rhetoric and media foundations precede advanced analysis and applied communication. Business and research gateways precede their dependent strategy, marketing, market research and leadership courses.
options.distinctness: The markets option adds economics, marketing, consumer product design, digital strategy, market research and leadership. These support analysis of organisations and audiences. The media and data option gives more weight to algorithms, data, language and media’s social effects.

options.label: Communication, organisation and interaction
options.labelReason: Social psychology, rhetoric, leadership and negotiation provide sustained study of influence and interaction. Qualitative and quantitative methods support inquiry into communication within organisations.
options.concept: Study how people make meaning, influence others and interact in organisations. Use social psychology and rhetoric to examine persuasion, then apply those ideas to leadership, negotiation and group decisions.
progression: Rhetoric and social psychology precede advanced influence and organisational study. The research gateway precedes dependent leadership and negotiation courses. Brain and behaviour precedes psycholinguistics and later psychology.
options.distinctness: This option adds social psychology, experimental methods, negotiation, leadership and lifespan study. The media and data option centres media forms and computational methods, while the markets option centres consumer decisions and strategy.

analysis: The closest option combines communication analysis, media history, narratives and representation, digital publics, and practical data methods. Media Archaeology supplies material and historical context, and Film & Text compares audiovisual and literary techniques. From T.V. to TikTok studies American mainstream media, including social platforms, and Media & Race supplies direct critical representation work. Data Science contributes data handling and visualisation, Database Management Systems contributes SQL and relational organisation, Machine Learning adds prediction and classification, and Image Processing & Computer Vision adds image filtering and segmentation. None alone delivers the dedicated humanistic platform and infographic analysis in the selected Utrecht package. AI Ethics strengthens privacy, fairness, responsibility and the social implications of AI. Psycholinguistics supports language processing and cognition within its description. The market option gives greater weight to market evidence, audience and consumer behaviour, product design, economics and business strategy. Strategy & Digital Transformation develops actual strategic planning, and Market Research conducts research and analyses findings. Leadership work supplies an organisation context. The interaction option joins social psychology, psycholinguistics, style, persuasion and experimental and qualitative inquiry to leadership, negotiation, emotion and organisational behaviour. Negotiation & Strategic Thinking adds bargaining simulations, framing and stakeholder interests in place of the weak clinical emphasis of Psychopathology. Medical and developmental psychology remain complementary contexts for behaviour and interaction. Systematic review is a bounded contribution and not an empirical capstone. The options differ pairwise by ten, eleven and ten courses in each direction. The official fourth culture and diversity package has substantive analogues in Media & Race, media narratives, identity and organisational inclusion. The first three official directions use the available comparison positions. Their content already represents related cultural questions without claiming Utrecht’s dedicated language-diversity sequence.

candidateDecisions.label: Culture, communication and diversity
candidateDecisions.reason: Utrecht’s fourth package is a valid direction. UCR can study representation and identity through Media & Race, media narratives, social theory, rhetoric and diversity in organisations. The first three listed packages already supply three distinct options. Culture and diversity overlaps the selected options through those shared courses.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce frameworks for analysing communication and its effects.
Both analyse meaning across text and audiovisual forms. UCR focuses on literary adaptation and film.
Both analyse language in interaction, including dialogue and pragmatic choices. Utrecht adds dedicated conversation analysis.
Both examine influence and the design of more effective messages.
Both examine AI’s effects and ethical implications. Utrecht focuses on how AI processes and generates language, while UCR studies a broader range of AI applications.
Both develop academic writing, argument and presentation. UCR also covers broader personal development.
Both introduce media institutions, forms and their relationship with society.
Both examine how media technologies develop and reshape communication, though UCR is more historically oriented.
Both consider media production, representation and participation on digital platforms. UCR situates those issues within American mainstream media.
Utrecht connects platform practices, datafication and social change. UCR treats related questions across media and social theory courses.
Both develop empirical research design, data collection, analysis and interpretation; UCR emphasises qualitative methodology.
Utrecht requires a proposal and research design for the thesis. UCR offers separate coursework in research design and systematic review.
Both teach ways to visualise information. UCR applies data visualisation across topics, while Utrecht also studies infographic design, cognition and interpretation.
Utrecht studies theories and politics of information. UCR covers data handling, media history and information systems across courses.
Both use computational analysis. UCR develops machine-learning methods, while Utrecht applies digital research and critical AI literacy to media and communication.
Utrecht requires an individual empirical research project and report. UCR offers optional independent research separately.
The comparator's 60-EC profiling space remains open, including its coherent 30-EC package requirement.
